newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGB futures slump with Nikkei, euroyen down.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGB futures slump with Nikkei, euroyen down.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese Government Bond (JGBs) futures came into focus on Tuesday in otherwise subdued pre-Christmas trade, dealers said.
Sentiment weakened early after the Bank of Japan cut the amount of its outright bond purchases, and prices eased further as the Nikkei 225 index skidded to 12-month lows.
The key March contract closed at 125.62, down from its previous settlement on December 20 at 126.15. The market brushed a low of 125.42 before rebounding in mid-afternoon.
SIMEX shut trading in JGB futures and Nikkei stock index futures on Monday due to a public holiday in Japan.
Euroyen futures were unchanged to lower on profit taking, paring gains triggered earlier by a drop in Tokyo stock prices.
But traders said the uptrend was intact as further weakness in Japan's economy reinforced views that Japan would retain its current low-rate policy into the near-term.
March Euroyen finished at 99.46, unchanged against the IMM and down one-tick from earlier in the day.
June Euroyen ended at 99.41, also unchanged against its previous IMM close.
"The Nikkei's sharp fall today signals a low interest rate policy. This should give euroyen more support," a dealer said.
Eurodollar futures ended little moved on an absence of new leads, with overnight U.S. data having scant impact.
A 0.5 percent rise in U.S. personal income in November, with spending up 0.5 percent, was construed as non-inflationary and unlikely to encourage a tighter credit environment.
The market spent the day mostly in a lull with institutions squaring positions ahead of year-end book closures.
The March contract finished at 94.45, unchanged against its IMM close, and June also ended unchanged at 94.31.
